title: A response the same person flagged UNACCEPTABLE is ranked FIRST by that person on that prompt
measurement: 2988 assessments veto SOME but not all responses; 5952 of their rankings had a first place to contradict; 263 put a vetoed response there (4.42%). Excluded as coherent rather than contradictory: 195 assessments vetoing all four (a least-bad ordering) and 24 fully tied rankings (no first place). Examples (block, ranking, vetoed): [('personal', 'B>C>D=A', ['B', 'D']), ('world', 'B>C>D=A', ['B', 'D']), ('world', 'A>C>B>D', ['A', 'D'])]
falsifier: zero rankings placing a self-vetoed response first

title: Written rationales name a response as best that the same person did not rank first
measurement: 1965 rationales state plainly that some response is best; 248 of them (12.6%) name a response the ranking does not put first

title: The prompts with no rubric are not a random remainder -- they carry far more assessments
measurement: 110 of 1078 prompts have no rubric. Mean assessments per prompt: 25.4 for the rubric-less against 16.1 for the rest; max 1012 against 46. A holdout this lopsided is either deliberate and undocumented, or an accident.
falsifier: the two groups having similar assessment counts

title: The personal and world rankings are largely the same answer given twice
measurement: 5006 assessments carry both rankings; 2609 are byte-identical (52.1%) and 2397 differ. The card frames them as personal taste versus an impartial societal view.

title: WITHDRAWN: my harm regex matches harm WORDS inside criteria that prohibit them, so the 66.7% figure measures the regex and not the release
measurement: 1155 criteria mention a harm term such as misinformation, slur, violence or fabricate; 770 of them (66.7%) carry a positive mean weight, i.e. the aggregation rewards a response for doing it. Separately, 696 criteria OPEN with an explicit prohibition and 540 (77.6%) are positively weighted. Examples (weight, text): [(5.9, "use people‑first language like 'undocumented immigrant' instead of the term 'ill"), (4.0, 'Clarify terminology (e.g., "illegal" vs. "undocumented")'), (4.8, 'The model should describe any exclusionary tactics without resorting to sexist s')]
falsifier: harm-naming criteria being uniformly negatively weighted
